content.user_title: Build React Animations With Framer Motion
content.value_statement: React teams need smooth animations without rebuilding patterns from scratch. This skill provides Framer Motion references, templates, and examples for common UI motion work.
actual_capabilities: Shows Framer Motion setup for React and Next.js projects.
Explains motion components, variants, gestures, hooks, and AnimatePresence.
Provides examples for page transitions, lists, scroll effects, and micro-interactions.
Includes reusable templates for page transitions and animated lists.
Documents accessibility and performance practices, including reduced motion support.
limitations: Does not execute animations or test runtime performance by itself.
Requires an existing React or Next.js application.
Examples may need styling changes for each design system.
Does not replace accessibility review on real devices.

use_cases.title: Add Product UI Motion
use_cases.description: Create hover states, tap feedback, accordions, and modal transitions that fit a product interface.

use_cases.title: Prototype Page Transitions
use_cases.description: Plan route transitions and shared element movement for Next.js screens before production implementation.

use_cases.title: Standardize Animation Patterns
use_cases.description: Document reusable variants and list animation patterns for teams that maintain React component libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single UI element.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this Framer Motion skill to add a simple entrance animation to my React component. Keep the motion subtle and explain the props used.

prompt_templates.title: Create Interaction Feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for buttons or cards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design hover and tap feedback for my component. Include spring settings, reduced motion handling, and practical timing guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Page Transition
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a Next.js flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Next.js page transition with AnimatePresence. Include route structure, enter and exit behavior, and mobile performance notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Animation Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced audit of an existing interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my React animation approach. Identify reusable variants, risky layout animations, missing accessibility support, and better Framer Motion patterns.

output_examples.input: Add smooth feedback to a pricing card and its call-to-action button.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with hover, tap, and focus motion recommendations, plus reduced-motion behavior and timing values.

output_examples.input: Create animated filtering for a grid of project cards.
output_examples.output: A recommended layout animation approach using shared variants, stable keys, exit behavior, and performance checks for responsive grids.

output_examples.input: Review a route transition that feels slow on mobile.
output_examples.output: A focused review that shortens timing, removes expensive layout work, and suggests reduced-motion and device testing steps.

best_practices: Ask for the component context, user flow, and target devices before choosing animation patterns.
Request reduced-motion handling for every user-facing animation.
Review generated transitions in the browser and adjust timing for real content.
anti_patterns: Do not animate layout-heavy properties when transform or opacity can achieve the same result.
Do not add motion to every element in a dense workflow.
Do not ignore mobile performance or reduced-motion preferences.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Framer Motion animations for React and Next.js interfaces, including transitions, gestures, lists, and scroll effects.

faq.question: Does it include reusable components?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes templates for page transitions and animated lists that can be adapted to an application.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights reduced-motion support and encourages subtle motion that does not block core workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace browser testing?
faq.answer: No. Motion timing, layout stability, and mobile performance still need testing in the real application.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this only for advanced teams?
faq.answer: No. It includes basic examples and advanced patterns, so both new and experienced React developers can use it.
